author: r. h. wasson
title: Rob Menendez highlights student visits and congressional oversight concerns in recent tweets
text:
Rep. Rob Menendez, U.S. Congressman representing New Jersey’s 8th district since 2023, shared updates on his official Twitter account this week about recent community engagements and congressional oversight efforts.
On June 8, Menendez posted about a visit from local students: “It’s always great meeting students to say hello. Thanks to Cordero Community School for stopping by to take a tour of the Capitol and hope you had a great trip to DC!”
Later that day, he addressed an incident involving congressional oversight at Delaney Hall: “Over the weekend, @SenatorAndyKim was blocked from speaking to individuals inside Delaney Hall. ICE & the GEO Group are doing everything they can to block congressional oversight & evade accountability. We will keep showing up & fighting to tell the stories of those inside,” (June 8).
On June 9, Menendez highlighted pediatric healthcare in New Jersey: “Nearly 90,000 kids from New Jersey visit @ChildrensPhila each year, including Adam, who I got to meet last week. Because of early detection and cutting-edge intervention for his condition, Adam is able to go to school, keep up with his peers, and school me in space facts.”
Rob Menendez has served as representative for New Jersey’s 8th District since succeeding Albio Sires in 2023. Born in Hudson County in 1985 and currently residing in Jersey City, Menendez holds degrees from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (BA) and Rutgers University-Newark (JD). His recent posts reflect ongoing engagement with both educational communities and issues related to immigration detention oversight.
